newsitem.title: UK: SIB's Large welcomes new super financial regulator.
newsitem.headline: SIB's Large welcomes new super financial regulator.

text.p: The outgoing chairman of Britain's Securities and Investments Board (SIB) said on Thursday the planned creation of super regulator is an "exciting opportunity of a kind that comes only once in a lifetime".
Large, writing in the SIB's annual report, conceded that the current two tier system is flawed and had led to duplication, inefficiency and delay.

Large is to be replaced by current Bank of England deputy governor Howard Davies who will head a regulator which will merge banking supervision, currently undertaken by the BOE, with the three front-line self-regulatory organisations which cover personal investments, the investment industry and the financial markets.

Sir Andrew said that examples of the current system's failings include delays to the review of the pensions industry and difficulties in following up the consequences of major management failures in cases such as the collapse of Barings and the problems at Morgan Grenfell Asset management.
"Following up the consequences of major management failures...has been made more difficult by the need to co-ordinate the policies and actions of separate organisations," Large writes.
